title: Short Stuff: Paperclips
summary: Short Stuff episode on the history of the paper clip. Josh and Chuck cover pre-paper-clip ribbon binding, the late-19th-century inventors (Samuel B. Fay's 1867 patent, Earlman J. Wright's 1877 improvement), the Gem paper clip attributed to Johan Vaaler of Norway (misspelled in transcript as Vohler/Volor; the name is Johan Vaaler), the Gem machine patent by William Middlebrook and the Gem company in the UK, the Norwegian resistance use of paper clips in WWII, the Oslo statue and 1999 stamp, and alternative designs like the Gothic clip and regal clip. Also touches on everyday paper clip uses and frustrations.
topics: BI Business School paper clip statue

segments.title: Opening banter and sponsor shout-outs
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the Short Stuff, thank sponsors and universities, and tease the messy history of the paper clip.

segments.title: Ribbon binding before paper clips
segments.summary: Before paper clips, people bound paper by slitting pages and threading ribbon through them. Late-19th-century inventors, around the same time and independently, began using mass-produced wire for paper binding.

segments.title: Early paper clip inventors Fay and Wright
segments.summary: Samuel B. Fay was the first to patent a bent wire paper clip, in 1867. Earlman J. Wright received an 1877 patent for an improvement on Fay's design, which resembled an awareness lapel pin.

segments.title: Hosts' eye-poking banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke about the danger of pointy objects and the risk of poking eyes with paper clips, including Josh's fear of sharp corners.

segments.title: Gem paper clip and Middlebrook's machine patent
segments.summary: The Gem paper clip, named after the Gem Manufacturing Company in the UK, was developed in 1899 with William Middlebrook of Connecticut. The company patented the machine that made it rather than the clip itself, so anyone with the resources could make it without paying royalties.

segments.title: Shout-out to listener Britta Phillips
segments.summary: Chuck mentions that Britta Phillips, bassist of Luna, is reportedly a listener. The hosts note she voiced Jim in the cartoon Jim and the Holograms, a reference to the Jim paper clip name confusion.

segments.title: Paper clip uses, flaws, and alternative designs
segments.summary: Paper clips are used to bind paper and to press reset buttons, and they can rust, tangle, poke, and stretch out. Companies still receive letters with fix ideas. Chuck describes spiral and regal clips, and Josh describes the Gothic clip, which has inverted angles so it does not poke through paper and is favored by archivists.

segments.title: Johan Vaaler, Norway, and the paper clip statue
segments.summary: Johan Vaaler is credited as the Norwegian inventor of the paper clip, though he did not get a patent in Norway and was credited through a 1920s German newspaper error. Norwegians wore paper clips as a symbol of resistance during Nazi occupation. A 23-foot statue at BI Business School in Oslo and a 1999 Norwegian stamp honor him, though the design shown is a Gem clip.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh wraps up the paper clip episode and Chuck gives the iHeartRadio production credit.
